description: Splits phase-2 (hard) round time into draft-side vs target-side wall-clock, to test whether GammaTune's draft-side savings are masked by a roughly-constant target-side cost per round.
interpretation: Confirms the hypothesis directionally: the adaptive controller cuts draft-side compute substantially (37.8%) in the hard phase, but target-side time does not shrink -- it is actually very slightly higher under adaptive (-5.7%, i.e. adaptive's target time is 5.7% MORE than fixed's), plausibly because adaptive runs more, smaller rounds (more separate target_verify calls, each paying the same fixed per-call cost) than fixed gamma=5 does. Target-side time (~1.1s) is roughly on par with or larger than draft-side time in both configs, and it does not decrease with a smaller gamma, so the achievable end-to-end speedup is capped well below the draft-side savings -- consistent with the ~8-9% overall speedup measured in p5_gamma_tune_speedup.py and p5_fluctuation_scenario.py rather than anything close to 37.8%.
